title: Marcar un antes y un después: un punto de inflexión histórico

sections.content: Marcar un antes y un después (to mark a turning point, to divide history into a before and after) describes an event so significant that everything afterward gets measured relative to it -- a vivid, idiomatic way to signal major historical significance. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Aquella noche marcaría un antes y un después para el conjunto del sistema internacional.
items.english: That night would mark a turning point for the entire international system.

items.spanish: Los gobiernos comunistas cayeron, marcando un antes y un después en un sistema que parecía inamovible.
items.english: The communist governments fell, marking a turning point in a system that had seemed unshakeable.

items.spanish: Estos acontecimientos de 1989 marcarían también un antes y un después en la relación de la región con las grandes potencias.
items.english: These events of 1989 would also mark a turning point in the region's relationship with the great powers.

items.spanish: Pocos acontecimientos del siglo veinte marcaron un antes y un después tan claro como la caída del Muro de Berlín.
items.english: Few twentieth-century events marked as clear a turning point as the fall of the Berlin Wall.

sections.content: This phrase works as a fixed unit -- marcar un antes y un después -- and doesn't split apart or take a direct object the way a literal reading might suggest; it's used almost like an intransitive expression describing the event's overall significance.
